item.title: These Are All English Words
item.description: A few weeks ago I showed a professor the latest developments of the framework we are building together. Among them was something I was rather proud of: an MCP server, a layer that lets a language model use the framework directly, building models, running analyses, reading results. (How I stumbled upon MCP, and what it has been like to build one, deserves a post of its own.) He scrolled through the code for a while, frowned, and said: “But these are all English words.”

item.title: Who Else Read My Proposal?
item.description: It is no secret that this year I resubmitted my MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal. Unfortunately, it does not reflect what is happening in the world right now, something I touched on briefly in my previous post and plan to come back to here soon. Still, the resubmission left me with a thought I cannot shake off.

item.title: The Elephant in the Session Room
item.description: Five days in Berlin for ECEE 2026, and what lingers is not a talk but a feeling of unease. Not because of the science: the science was excellent. Professor Cotton’s keynote on ground-motion models in the age of big data was among the most stimulating talks I have heard in a while, and Professor Vamvatsikos confirmed once again his gift for metaphors that are daring and yet pedagogically flawless (I deeply regret never having sat in one of his classes as a student).
